[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".
